summary: The appellants alleged post-operative medical negligence and inadequate follow-up care leading to the death of Naveen Kant after a kidney transplant performed on 12th November 1995. The National Consumer Disputes Redressal Commission dismissed the complaint, finding no medical negligence. The Supreme Court upheld this decision, noting that the evidence, including expert testimony, lacked credibility as the doctors cited were not nephrologists. The Court emphasized that complications post-surgery, despite best efforts, do not automatically constitute negligence. The patient’s deteriorating condition due to infection and septicemia was tragic but did not demonstrate a lack of standard care.
legal_provisions_cited: Transplantation of Human Organs and Tissues Act, 1994
